question_text: Under which of the following conditions in-vitro-in-vivo correlation for a drug fails?

options.A: When the drug is highly soluble
options.B: When the drug's absorption takes place by a complex process
options.C: When the dissolution medium is adequately simulated
options.D: When the drug is highly permeable but poorly soluble

explanation: Complex absorption processes (e.g., active transport or carrier-mediated influx/efflux) complicate the relationship between simple in vitro dissolution and in vivo absorption.

question_text: Which of the following levels of IVIVC is represented by "the relationship between one dissolution time point (e.g. t 50%) and one mean pharmacokinetic parameter, such as AUC, $T_{max}$ or $C_{max}$"?
explanation: Level C IVIVC establishes a single-point relationship between a dissolution parameter and a pharmacokinetic parameter.

question_text: During determination of absorption rate constant by method of residual, flip-flop phenomenon occurs when ($K_a$ absorption rate constant and $K_E$ overall elimination rate constant).
explanation: The flip-flop phenomenon occurs when the apparent absorption rate constant is actually the elimination rate constant, which happens when $K_E / K_a$ is significantly large ($K_E / K_a \ge 3$).
